stem: In a circle with center $M$, $\overline{AB}$ and $\overline{CD}$ are two chords. $MX\perp\overline{AB}$ at $X$ and $MY\perp\overline{CD}$ at $Y$, where $MX=MY={=d}$ cm and $CD={=L}$ cm. Then $AB=\ldots$ cm
solution: MX and MY are the distances from the center M to the chords AB and CD.
MX = MY = {=d} cm, so the two chords are equidistant from the center.
By the converse of the theorem, AB = CD.
notes: Basic: direct use of the converse, no figure needed (the distances are given in words).
